name: Axe of the Dwarven Lords

currentBonuses.when: while the axe is in your possession, when Crafting armor, jewelry, metalwork, stonemasonry, snares, traps, or weapons
on Strikes with the axe against orcs

evidence: "you gain a +4 item bonus when Crafting armor, jewelry, metalworking, stonemasonry, snares, traps, and weapons" — limited to that list of Craft subjects; and "Strikes with the axe deal an additional 1d6 damage to orcs".

corrections.problem: The classification (+4 item to the listed Craft subjects, +1d6 vs orcs) is correct and the engineNote rightly calls out that passiveEffects.skills.crafting = 4 over-applies a subject-restricted bonus to every Crafting check. But it misses a second, identical over-application in the same record: passiveEffects.senses grants "greater darkvision" unconditionally, while the text says "If you are a dwarf, you gain greater darkvision while holding the axe. If you are not a dwarf, you are Stupefied 4 while holding the axe" — so a non-dwarf carrying the axe currently gets free greater darkvision and none of the penalties.
corrections.correction: Extend the engineNote to cover the sense: greater darkvision is gated on being a dwarf AND holding the axe, and the non-dwarf/orc penalties (stupefied 4, drained 4, enfeebled 4) are unmodelled. Neither is expressible with the listed target kinds, so this is an engine/data note, not a new bonus entry.

name: Glorious Banner

currentBonuses.when: to AC while your commander's banner is up and you're in its aura
to Fortitude saves while your commander's banner is up and you're in its aura
to Reflex saves while your commander's banner is up and you're in its aura

evidence: "you and affected allies gain a +1 status bonus to AC, Fortitude saves, and Reflex saves"

corrections.problem: The engineNote states as settled fact that the Will-vs-fear increase is 'granted to your allies' and therefore out of reach for this sheet. That is only one reading. The base class feature it modifies (classFeatures/commanders-banner) says the aura 'gives you and all allies in a a +1 status bonus to Will saves and DCs against fear effects' — the commander explicitly DOES receive the base +1. Whether Glorious Banner raises the commander's own bonus to +2 is genuinely ambiguous (the same sentence's next clause switches to 'you and affected allies', which cuts the other way), so it should not be closed off with needsHumanDecision:false. The three marked bonuses (+1 status to AC / Fortitude / Reflex) are correct.
corrections.correction: Keep the three AC/Fort/Reflex entries as-is, but set needsHumanDecision:true with the question: 'Commander's Banner gives the +1 status vs fear to "you and all allies"; does Glorious Banner's increase to +2 apply to the commander's own Will saves/DCs vs fear, or literally only to allies?' Also worth recording in the note that the commander's own baseline +1 status to Will saves vs fear lives on classFeatures/commanders-banner, which the feats-only lookup can never reach.

If you were already trained in Warfare Lore, you become trained in a Lore skill of your choice.' — so every character who can take Siege Ritualist is guaranteed to have Warfare Lore. corrections.correction: Replace the engineNote's second sentence with: 'Warfare Lore is always present — War Mage Dedication, the prerequisite, grants the Additional Lore feat for Warfare Lore — so the star will always render once the app models that grant.'

name: Guiding Shot
evidence: "If the Strike hits, the next creature other than you to attack the same target before the start of your next turn gains a +1 circumstance bonus to their roll, or a +2 circumstance bonus if your Strike was a critical hit."

corrections.problem: The engineNote's factual claim is false: 'there are two records with this id text in core.json (Player Core and Battlecry! printings) with identical wording'. There is exactly one record keyed guiding-shot, source 'Pathfinder Battlecry!' — no duplicate exists in any collection. The classification (situational:false, ally-only, 'the next creature other than you') is correct.
corrections.correction: Drop the duplicate-record sentence from the engineNote; keep only the ally-targeted-buff-lane gap.

corrections.problem: The classification is right but the engineNote is factually wrong: it claims "there are two records with this id text in core.json (Player Core and Battlecry! printings) with identical wording". core.json contains exactly ONE record with id "guiding-shot" (verified: a single match for the literal `"id":"guiding-shot"`, and a single occurrence of the sentence "Your ranged attack helps guide your allies into striking your enemy's weak point"). Acting on the note would send an implementer hunting for a duplicate key that does not exist.
corrections.correction: The second, near-identically-worded record is a DIFFERENT feat: `assisting-shot` — "Assisting Shot", level 2, category class, traits ["fighter","press"], source Pathfinder Player Core, sharing the tail "If the Strike hits, the next creature other than you to attack the same target before the start of your next turn gains a +1 circumstance bonus to their roll, or a +2 circumstance bonus if your Strike was a critical hit." `guiding-shot` itself is level 2, traits ["commander","flourish"], source Pathfinder Battlecry!, edition remaster-era. Replace the duplicate-id sentence with: "The fighter feat `assisting-shot` shares this wording and is likewise ally-only (situational:false) — it needs the same ally-targeted buff lane."

name: Great Shield Mastery

currentBonuses.bonus: +4 circumstance (the shield's Take Cover value) instead of the usual +2
currentBonuses.when: to AC whenever you have a tower shield, fortress shield, or similar raised — you get the Take Cover benefit for free

evidence: "You continually benefit from Take Cover without needing to spend an action, as long as you have a shield raised and it's a tower shield, fortress shield, or other shield that grants a higher circumstance bonus to AC when you Take Cover behind it."

corrections.problem: The bonus string '+4 circumstance (the shield's Take Cover value) instead of the usual +2' hard-codes a baseline that is only right for a tower shield. In core.json tower-shield has acBonus 2 (description: 'AC increases to +4 if you are using the Take Cover action') but fortress-shield has acBonus 3, and its description gives no number at all ('Getting the higher bonus for this shield requires using the Take Cover action while the shield is raised'). The feat text itself never states any number, so 'the usual +2' is an invented constant for one of the two shields the feat names.
corrections.correction: Phrase the magnitude shield-relative, e.g. bonus: 'your raised shield's higher Take Cover AC value (tower shield: +4 instead of +2)' with the engineNote already-correct point that the number must be read off the equipped shield and REPLACES rather than stacks with the raised-shield circumstance bonus.

corrections.problem: Under-reports the benefit and closes the question it should have left open. The feat text is confirmed — "You continually benefit from Take Cover without needing to spend an action, as long as you have a shield raised and it's a tower shield, fortress shield, or other shield that grants a higher circumstance bonus to AC when you Take Cover behind it" — but the spec records AC only, with needsHumanDecision:false. core.json's own `take-cover` action record says the benefit is not AC-only: "If you would have standard cover, you instead gain greater cover, which provides a +4 circumstance bonus to AC; to Reflex saves against area effects; and to Stealth checks to hide, sneak, or otherwise avoid detection. Otherwise, you gain standard cover (a +2 circumstance bonus instead)." A permanently-on Take Cover therefore plausibly also boosts Reflex-vs-area and Stealth, and neither is mentioned.
corrections.correction: Keep situational:true and the AC entry, but set needsHumanDecision:true with the question: "Great Shield Mastery grants continual Take Cover. core.json's Take Cover record gives a circumstance bonus to AC, to Reflex saves against area effects, and to Stealth to Hide/Sneak, whereas the Tower Shield item record only says 'AC increases to +4 if you are using the Take Cover action'. Does a raised tower/fortress shield confer the full cover package (add save/reflex and skill/stealth entries) or only the shield's AC increase?" Also correct the bonus string's provenance: the '+4' is read off the tower-shield item, and the '+2' it is contrasted with is the standard-cover value from the Take Cover record — not, as the note implies, purely the raised-shield bonus; the magnitude still has to come from the equipped shield, which the fixed-string shape cannot express.

corrections.correction: Set needsEngineWork false and drop the union complaint from engineNote (keep the note that quickened / Drained 2 / Stupefied 2 are conditions, not bonuses). corrections.problem: The condition string misstates the timing: "while Stage 1 of plasma hype is active (1 round after you Interact to take it)" reads as a one-round delay before the bonus arrives. The record lists no Onset (unlike grolna, which explicitly has "**Onset** 1 minute"); the "(1 round)" in "**Stage 1** +10-foot status bonus to speed, quickened... (1 round)" is the DURATION of stage 1, which begins immediately. A player reading the star would wait a round for a bonus they already had, and would not know it expires when stage 2 begins.
corrections.correction: Keep situational true, targetKind 'speed', "+10-foot status" (all correct per the text). Rephrase when to: "while Stage 1 of plasma hype lasts — 1 round, starting immediately when you Interact to take it; Stage 2 drops the Speed bonus and keeps only quickened". Everything else in the spec (status type, the quickened/Drained 2/Stupefied 2 riders being conditions rather than bonuses) checks out.

name: Astrolabe

currentBonuses.when: on checks to identify celestial bodies (astrolabe held in two hands; the standard model works only on steady ground)

evidence: "An astrolabe also grants a +1 item bonus to checks to identify celestial bodies."

corrections.problem: The engineNote asserts as fact that the trained-in-Survival requirement "is attached to the Calculate activity, NOT to the identify-celestial-bodies bonus". The record does not say that — it states it flatly and unqualified: "To use an astrolabe, the holder must be trained in Survival." That sentence precedes the Calculate description and reads as a general gate on using the item. The spec's conclusion (do not bind the bonus to skill 'survival') is still right — being trained in Survival is a prerequisite, not the skill rolled — but the justification is invented and the 'when' string omits a stated requirement.
corrections.correction: Drop the "attached to the Calculate activity" claim from engineNote and add the prerequisite to the condition text: "on checks to identify celestial bodies, if you are trained in Survival (astrolabe held in two hands...)". Apply the same fix to astrolabe-standard and astrolabe-mariners, which share the identical sentence. Keep the needsHumanDecision question about which skill key to bind to. Minor: on the umbrella record the 'when' folds in "the standard model works only on steady ground", a restriction that belongs to the standard grade only.

corrections.problem: The engineNote misreads the record in a way that skews the human decision it raises. It claims the trained-in-Survival requirement "is attached to the Calculate activity, NOT to the identify-celestial-bodies bonus". The record says no such thing — its text is "To use an astrolabe, the holder must be trained in Survival.", a blanket requirement for using the item at all, stated before the navigation procedure and before "An astrolabe also grants a +1 item bonus to checks to identify celestial bodies." Nothing scopes it to Calculate. Survival is therefore a live candidate for the skill binding, not something that would be "reading in something the text does not say".
corrections.correction: The bonus itself is right: situational true, +1 item, targetKind 'skill' with the condition doing the work, needsHumanDecision true. Fix the engineNote to state that the record gates ALL use of the astrolabe on being trained in Survival, and re-frame the question as: "the text names no skill for 'checks to identify celestial bodies', but gates use of the item on Survival training — bind to survival, to a Lore, or leave as skill 'all' with the condition text?" Note also that skill 'all' does render today (targetMatches treats detail 'all' as matching any skill), so needsEngineWork false is correct.

name: Sovereign Steel Armor

currentBonuses.when: to AC against spell attack rolls, while wearing sovereign steel armor

evidence: "The noqual in sovereign steel armor provides protection against magic, granting you a +1 circumstance bonus to AC against spell attack rolls."

corrections.problem: Coverage is inverted across the sovereign-steel family. The material text — "All sovereign steel items (including weapon and armor below) ... grant their bonus to saves the owner makes specifically to protect the item from magic" — explicitly names armor, yet the +4 circumstance save leg is registered ONLY on the two Sovereign Steel Object records (raw material priced per Bulk, which the spec itself doubts should ever star) and NOT on the three armor records, which are the ones a character actually wears. The +1 circumstance AC vs spell attack rolls on the armor records is correct and verified.
corrections.correction: Decide one way and apply it consistently across sovereign-steel-armor, sovereign-steel-armor-standard-grade and sovereign-steel-armor-high-grade vs sovereign-steel-object-standard-grade / -high-grade: either add the "+4 circumstance, on a save you make specifically to protect this sovereign steel item from magic (e.g. vs. rusting grasp)" leg to the armor records too, or drop it from the Object records as an unrollable/GM-side effect. Note the armor records' own description text does not repeat the +4 clause (it lives on the material record), so if the rule is strict grounding in the record's own text, the Object entries are the ones to drop.

name: Dad Joke

currentBonuses.when: when you use Dad Joke and substitute a Lore check for the skill that would identify the target, if that Lore could identify it

evidence: you can instead attempt a Lore check with a +2 circumstance bonus if the target is trained in that Lore or could be identified by that Lore when Recalling Knowledge

corrections.problem: The condition is narrowed and the engineNote invents a Paizo typo that the text does not support. The record reads: 'you can instead attempt a Lore check with a +2 circumstance bonus if the target is trained in that Lore or could be identified by that Lore when Recalling Knowledge.' That is a DISJUNCTION with two qualifying branches. The spec's `when` keeps only the second branch ('if that Lore could identify it') and silently drops the first. The engineNote then asserts the first branch 'reads as a Paizo typo for "if you are trained in that Lore"' — that is an invented rewrite. The printed clause is coherent as written: Dad Joke is a lovingly tailored joke, so a Lore the TARGET is trained in (Farming Lore for a farmer) is exactly the kind of Lore you would build the pun from. Rewriting a printed condition on a typo hunch is the 'condition invented or broadened beyond what the text says' failure mode.
corrections.correction: Restore both printed branches and drop the typo claim. Use when: 'when you use Dad Joke and substitute a Lore check for the skill that would identify the target, if the target is trained in that Lore or that Lore could identify it'. Keep bonus '+2 circumstance', targetKind 'skill'. Keep needsEngineWork true, but restate the engine gap accurately: the registry keys Lore individually as `lore:*` (see the SituationalTarget doc comment in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts), so there is no key meaning 'whichever Lore fits the target'; skill 'lore' is a placeholder for a missing any-Lore target. If the typo reading is still suspected, that belongs in needsHumanDecision as a question, not applied as a silent edit to the condition.

corrections.problem: The condition was rewritten rather than recorded: the spec declares 'if the target is trained in that Lore' a Paizo typo for 'if you are trained in that Lore', then drops that whole branch from the condition text, leaving only 'if that Lore could identify it'. The record's actual text is "you can instead attempt a Lore check with a +2 circumstance bonus if the target is trained in that Lore or could be identified by that Lore when Recalling Knowledge" — two alternative branches joined by 'or'. The printed wording is not obviously a typo: a joke landing because the TARGET knows the subject (Blacksmithing Lore at a blacksmith) reads perfectly well for a feat literally called Dad Joke, and the second branch ('could be identified by that Lore') already covers the identification case, so the spec's rewrite makes the first branch redundant with the second. Emitting a condition that silently deletes half of a printed 'A or B' is the 'condition invented or broadened beyond what the text says' failure, in the narrowing direction. Secondary defect: target skill is 'lore', which is not a key the registry can match — situationalBonuses.ts documents skill detail as 'a skill key, a `lore:*` key, or `all`', so a bare 'lore' would match no skill and the star would never render.
corrections.correction: Set the when text to the printed rule, both branches: 'when you use Dad Joke and substitute a Lore check for the skill that would identify the target, if the target is trained in that Lore or could be identified by that Lore'. Move the typo hypothesis out of the data and into needsHumanDecision: 'The printed text says "if the target is trained in that Lore" — is that a Paizo typo for "if you are trained in that Lore", or does the target's own training genuinely qualify? I have kept the printed wording.' Keep needsEngineWork true and state the missing piece precisely: the registry has no 'any Lore' key (only concrete lore:* keys and 'all'), so skill:'lore' will not match anything as authored — either add an 'any lore' detail or use skill:'all' with the Lore-only condition spelled out.

name: Sharkskin Grip

currentBonuses.when: while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing, on unarmed attack rolls
while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing
while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing, to Escape, Grab an Edge, or avoid falling prone

evidence: As long as you're wearing your clothing, you gain a +1 item bonus to unarmed attack rolls, Acrobatics checks, and Reflex saves and DCs to Escape, Grab an Edge, or avoid falling prone.

corrections.problem: The needsHumanDecision question presents only two readings and omits the most likely one, so the Acrobatics row as written is probably over-broad. Text: '+1 item bonus to unarmed attack rolls, Acrobatics checks, and Reflex saves and DCs to Escape, Grab an Edge, or avoid falling prone.' The spec asks only 'does the qualifier scope the Reflex half, or all three?' — but the natural third reading is that it scopes the Acrobatics AND Reflex halves and leaves only unarmed attacks unqualified, because every action in the trailing list is an Acrobatics/Reflex action (Escape can be an Acrobatics check, Grab an Edge is a Reflex save, avoiding falling prone is Acrobatics or Reflex). Under the spec's chosen reading the sheet stars ALL Acrobatics while the clothing is worn, which is a broader claim than the sentence supports. Second problem: the engineNote suggests the unarmed-attack and Acrobatics halves 'could be treated as flat item bonuses in the maths instead of stars'. Doing that for unarmed attacks would be a real bug — Handwraps of Mighty Blows already supply an ITEM bonus to unarmed attacks, item bonuses do not stack, so folding this into the maths would silently inflate the strike total for any character with handwraps.
corrections.correction: Rewrite the question to offer three readings: (a) qualifier scopes only Reflex saves/DCs; (b) qualifier scopes Acrobatics and Reflex, leaving only unarmed attacks unconditional; (c) qualifier scopes all three. Flag (b) as the reading the sentence structure best supports, and until the owner rules, scope the Acrobatics entry with when: 'while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing, to Escape, Grab an Edge, or avoid falling prone' rather than the bare 'while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing'. Delete the suggestion to move any part of this into the maths, or replace it with an explicit warning that the unarmed-attack half must stay display-only because it is an item bonus that does not stack with Handwraps of Mighty Blows.

corrections.problem: The spec's chosen default reading broadens two of the three bonuses far beyond what the text supports. Record text: "you gain a +1 item bonus to unarmed attack rolls, Acrobatics checks, and Reflex saves and DCs to Escape, Grab an Edge, or avoid falling prone." The spec reads the trailing qualifier as scoping ONLY the Reflex clause, so it emits an unqualified '+1 item on unarmed attack rolls' and an unqualified '+1 item on all Acrobatics checks' (condition text is only 'while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing'). Core.json's own action records show why that is the wrong default: `escape` says "Attempt a check using your unarmed attack modifier... You can attempt an Acrobatics or Athletics check instead", and `grab-an-edge` says "You must succeed at your choice of an Acrobatics check or a Reflex save". Each of the three listed statistics is exactly a legal roll for one or more of the three listed actions — that is why they are listed together, and the qualifier scopes the whole list. The spec's reading also hands a level-4 archetype feat a permanent +1 item bonus to every unarmed Strike (equivalent to a +1 striking weapon) and to every Acrobatics check, which the near-always-true 'while wearing your clothing' condition would then park behind a star as if it were rare.
corrections.correction: Keep needsHumanDecision, but flip the default to the narrow reading. All three entries should carry the Escape/Grab an Edge/avoid-falling-prone qualifier: strikeAttack — '+1 item', when: 'while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing, on unarmed attack rolls to Escape'; skill/acrobatics — '+1 item', when: 'while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing, to Escape, Grab an Edge, or avoid falling prone'; save/reflex — '+1 item', when: 'while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing, to Grab an Edge or avoid falling prone (and to your Escape DC)'. Reword the question to: 'Does the trailing qualifier scope the whole list? The Escape and Grab an Edge action texts say each listed statistic is a legal roll for one of the listed actions, which is why I default to the narrow reading — confirm before we grant a blanket +1 item to unarmed attacks and Acrobatics.' Keep needsEngineWork for the Escape DC half.

name: Civil Service
evidence: You gain a +2 status bonus to New Leadership checks.

corrections.problem: `situational: false` is being used to mean 'out of scope' rather than its defined meaning ('unconditional, so it belongs in the maths'), and the chunk applies it inconsistently. Six records whose bonus lands on someone other than the character (fear-no-pain, swift-support, bounce-boost, personalized-poisoning, guardians-deflection-swashbuckler, snap-out-of-it-marshal) are marked situational TRUE with an empty bonus list, while eight Kingmaker records with the same 'nothing lands on a character stat' shape are marked situational FALSE with an empty list. Worse, several kingdom specs contradict their own flag: aon-fortified-fiefs is false yet its engineNote says 'within that subsystem both modifiers WOULD be situational', and aon-inspiring-entertainment is false yet its engineNote says 'within that subsystem this one is clearly situational'. aon-civil-service is the same case — '+2 status bonus to New Leadership checks' is restricted to one named kingdom activity, so it is conditional, not unconditional. A downstream reader taking `situational: false` at its documented meaning would conclude these are flat bonuses.
corrections.correction: Unify the two families on one encoding. Recommended: reserve `situational: false` for genuinely unconditional bonuses, and mark every 'nothing lands on a character statistic' record as situational true + bonuses [] + needsEngineWork true, with the reason (ally-facing / companion-facing / kingdom subsystem) in engineNote. Under that rule, flip aon-civil-service, aon-cooperative-leadership, aon-crush-dissent, aon-fortified-fiefs, aon-free-and-fair, aon-insider-trading and aon-inspiring-entertainment to situational true with empty bonuses. aon-practical-magic is the one kingdom record that should stay false, because '+1 status bonus to Magic checks' really is unconditional inside its own subsystem. Either way, remove the engineNote sentences that assert the opposite of the flag on the same record.

name: Harsh Judgement

currentBonuses.when: to Seek your condemned foe
to Demoralize your condemned foe
to Seek any creature other than your condemned foe
to Demoralize anyone other than your condemned foe

evidence: You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to Seek your condemned foe and on Intimidation checks to Demoralize them. You have a -1 circumstance penalty to Perception checks to Seek creatures other than your condemned foe and on Intimidation checks to Demoralize anyone other than your condemned foe.

corrections.problem: The engineNote contradicts the data it ships. It says 'the sheet must not present them as bonuses' while the two -1 circumstance penalties are placed in the `bonuses` array, which is exactly what the sheet renders as bonuses. name: Spell Swipe
evidence: "If you're using a weapon that has the sweep trait, its circumstance bonus applies against both targets."

corrections.problem: Marked situational:false with reasonIfNot "the feat merely extends that already-earned bonus to the second target". That mischaracterises the sweep trait. core.json's text is: "If you're using a weapon that has the sweep trait, its circumstance bonus applies against both targets." Sweep only gives its +1 circumstance bonus "against a target you already attempted to attack this turn"; a Spell Swipe rolls separate Strikes against TWO different creatures, so neither Strike would normally qualify. The feat therefore creates a bonus that would not otherwise exist — it is not an already-earned bonus being carried over. Classifying it as "nothing to star" drops a real conditional bonus (the exact under-coverage the lane exists to fix).
corrections.correction: situational: true, one entry — targetKind 'strikeAttack', bonus "+1 circumstance (your weapon's sweep bonus)", when "on both Strikes of a Spell Swipe when you're wielding a sweep weapon". needsEngineWork false; needsHumanDecision optional if the owner wants weapon-trait-derived bonus sizes resolved from the equipped weapon rather than printed as +1. Medium confidence: the deciding text is the sweep trait's own wording, which lives outside this record, so it is worth a second look by the app owner.
